nodes.label: Five-Stage Pipeline (Fetch, Clean, Store, Analyze, Render)
nodes.rationale: Stages are deliberately independent so a fetch failure does not block analysis of previously stored data; the dashboard reads from the DB so it can be regenerated without re-fetching. main.py orchestrates fetch-clean-store; scripts/generate_html.py orchestrates analyze-render.
nodes.norm_label: five-stage pipeline (fetch, clean, store, analyze, render)

nodes.label: Native Units, Convert at Display Rule
nodes.rationale: DB stores native exchange units (cents/bu, cents/lb, $/short ton); conversion to USD/MT happens only at display via pipeline/units. Round-tripping through MT introduces rounding error and makes the source of truth for downstream math ambiguous; a fixed storage unit gives every analysis function and test one obvious input space.
nodes.norm_label: native units, convert at display rule

nodes.label: One-Way Module Dependency Rule
nodes.rationale: Dependency direction is strictly one-way: fetchers never import pipeline or analysis; pipeline never imports analysis; analysis imports only pipeline/query and pipeline/units. Keeps layers independently evolvable and testable.

nodes.label: Turso-or-SQLite Storage Abstraction
nodes.rationale: pipeline/connection.py returns a Turso cloud connection when TURSO_DATABASE_URL is set, local SQLite otherwise; call sites don't care which. MIRROR_REQUIRE_TURSO=1 opts into strict mode so CI/production deploys don't silently fall back to local SQLite and mask a config bug.

nodes.label: 19-Layer Data Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Each of the 19 source layers is independent and wrapped in try/except so one failure never blocks the rest (graceful degradation); freshness is recorded after each successful layer. 14 of 19 layers run with zero API keys.

nodes.label: Briefing Package (orchestrator + 26 sections + BriefingData)
nodes.rationale: The 1,492-LOC briefing monolith was split into a package: one module per section exposing format(), an orchestrator that joins them, and a frozen BriefingData dataclass so consumers can render one section at a time. generate_briefing() is a thin wrapper returning BriefingData.text so existing callers keep working.

nodes.label: Front-Month Roll-Day Discontinuity (Known Limitation)
nodes.rationale: yfinance silently switches underlying contracts near expiry, creating artificial price gaps on roll days. Technicals and signals propagate the discontinuity; mitigation demotes signals within +/-3 business days of an estimated roll date to info severity tagged (near-roll). Spreads/basis largely cancel the artifact. Deferred fix: Panama-adjusted adj_close column with a dual-column read pattern (technicals adjusted, spreads/basis raw).

nodes.label: Anti-Bot Wall Layer Disablement (NCDEX + CEPEA)
nodes.rationale: Layer 16 (NCDEX) is blocked by a JS fingerprint interstitial (__hd_fingerprint cookie via /__verify/fp); Layer 17 (CEPEA) by a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge (HTTP 403). Both are short-circuited in main.py via _mark_empty with diagnostic logging so the wall is visible, and fetcher code is preserved. Re-enabling needs alternate sources or a Playwright bypass, not a URL update.

nodes.label: FetchResult Typed Fetch Outcome (ok/empty/failed)
nodes.rationale: Frozen dataclass with Literal status and three constructors. The three states each demand a different freshness row (success with rows, success with zero rows, failed); conflating them was the original sin behind 'the dashboard says everything is green but no exports loaded'.

nodes.label: ScraperShapeError Pattern
nodes.rationale: Raised by HTML scrapers when the upstream page no longer matches the expected structure, instead of returning empty DataFrames. Subclasses ValueError so existing except blocks still catch it, but lets the dashboard distinguish 'no data this week' from 'the scraper is broken'.

nodes.label: Shared retry_sleep Backoff with Jitter
nodes.rationale: Single exponential-backoff formula (capped 30s, 0-1s jitter) replacing nine copies of time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY). Jitter matters because the 18-layer pipeline otherwise produces synchronised retry storms against shared upstreams (USDA, FRED, EIA).

nodes.label: _mark_empty vs _mark_failed Freshness Distinction
nodes.rationale: _mark_failed writes status='failed' preserving prior last_success (powers 'last good run was N days ago'); _mark_empty writes status='success', rows_fetched=0 for legitimately-empty weeks. Before this, empty was indistinguishable from never-ran and failed from succeeded.

nodes.label: Stocks-to-Use Ratio Signal
nodes.rationale: Ending-stocks / total-use per commodity with detect_tight_supply() flagging bottom-decile years. Sourced from the PSD frame rather than direct WASDE numbers because NASS QuickStats does not expose ending stocks and total use in a stable queryable shape; PSD carries both country-keyed with WASDE-consistent definitions.

nodes.label: Shared Z-Score Helpers (COT + Weather)
nodes.rationale: zscore(series, window) and format_zscore(z) factored out of two callers rolling their own. COT section flags positioning at |z| >= 2 instead of a fixed net-position threshold that missed regime shifts in low-OI contracts; weather section annotates anomaly z-scores alongside threshold breaches.

nodes.label: Brazil Export Basis (compute_brazil_basis)
nodes.rationale: CBOT (USD/MT) vs CEPEA/AgRural (USD/MT after BRL FX conversion). Negative basis = Brazilian beans below CBOT in dollar terms (export-competitive discount). AgRural Paranagua FOB was added because CEPEA covers interior spot while the export-basis question is about FOB-at-port; the two differ by the inland-freight wedge.

nodes.label: Briefing Archive (briefings table + snapshot_json)
nodes.rationale: Every briefing run persists text plus a structured snapshot_json distilled from BriefingData. Enables backtesting questions like 'what did we say last Tuesday when the dollar broke 105' without re-running against a moved-on database, and unblocks signal recall@N analysis before promoting new rules to alert severity.

nodes.label: CONAB Fetcher Schema Rewrite (Layer 15)
nodes.rationale: CONAB switched SerieHistoricaGraos.txt to a semicolon-separated per-UF schema; the old fetcher silently parsed it as one column and every row was discarded. Rewrite parses sep=';', aggregates 27 UF rows to national totals, recomputes yield from aggregated production/area, and hard-fails with logger.error listing received columns if the schema drifts again.

nodes.label: Batch executemany Upsert Refactor
nodes.rationale: Replaced 19 per-row iterrows writers with one batch executemany helper inside a transaction: 7.5-8.5x speedup and store.py halved (979 to 471 LOC). Freshness and save_wasde defaulting logic kept verbatim because they carry non-trivial business rules.

nodes.label: Soybean Crush Spread
nodes.rationale: Processing margin: (Oil x 11) + (Meal x 2.2) - Beans. Positive = profitable to crush; widening spread = processors buying more beans = price support. oil_value_share extension crosses 50% during biofuel-pull regimes and answers 'is the board paying for beans or for oil'.

nodes.label: Market Drivers Narrative
nodes.rationale: Connects dots across data sources that no single section shows alone: BRL + exports, COT + RSI crowding, weather + price premium, dollar strength, corn/soy acreage competition, livestock feed demand, China export-sales share, forward curve structure.

nodes.label: Trader-Grade Signals Suite
nodes.rationale: Signals modelled on metrics commodity desks actually watch, not generic technicals: stocks-to-use, Brazil basis, soy-oil value share, COT and weather z-scores, and the briefing archive for backtesting. Snapshot caveat: basis, stocks-to-use, and z-scores render in the text briefing but are not yet in snapshot_json.

nodes.label: Mirror Market Design System (Industrial Dark)
nodes.rationale: Bloomberg Terminal meets modern developer tools, aimed at defense-tech hiring managers viewing the repo as a portfolio piece. GitHub dark palette chosen over pure black for dense-data readability; Geist typography to signal engineering craft over template dashboards; dark-only because trading desks use dark themes; minimal decoration so typography and color hierarchy do the visual work; fixed sidebar for persistent nav plus data freshness at a glance.

nodes.label: Fixtures-as-Snapshots Policy
nodes.rationale: Committed HTML/CSV fixtures let scraper tests run without the network. When the live site changes shape, the parser raises ScraperShapeError while tests keep passing against the frozen fixture — that divergence IS the alert. Re-capture only after the parser is updated for the new shape.
